directive: Move the kernel to Stat and rebuild it around exact realized-degree support: for N>=1 define delta_N=1/N when N is even and delta_N=1/(2N) when N is odd, set h_i(h)=max{h,delta_{N_i}}, and use the exact normalized score at h_i(h); set it to zero only for N_i=0. Replace C_pc L h^2 by a graph-observable certificate containing L(6n)^(-1) sum_{N_i>0} h_i(h)^2 + B n^(-1) sum_i 1{N_i=0}, plus the proved PC remainder, and derive the corresponding degree-exact variance bound. Then, without changing the current i.i.d. (U_i,f_i) class or conditioning convention, compute a same-class testing modulus for unsupported units and low-degree tails: include only its proved order in both minimax lower bounds and the revised phase diagram, and do not promote the safe B-times-isolated-fraction upper bound to a lower bound without indistinguishable witnesses. Keep theta_n as a new finite-population derivative target and describe Li-Wager Theorem 6 only as an asymptotic benchmark through an explicit Proposition-1 bridge, not a same-target tightening; also correct or remove the mischaracterized Bhadra-Schweinberger entry. If the unsupported-unit modulus cannot be matched while retaining the stated class, withdraw the matched-frontier theorem rather than adding minimum-degree or response-sharing assumptions.

Revise only prop:linear-special-case into a predeclared zero-remainder sanity reduction: state it on the nested class M_{n,d,0} subseteq M_{n,d,L}, noting that affine responses are a special case and that the exact score also cancels quadratic responses. Evaluate def:radii and the bandwidth rule with the sharp class radius L=0; then the positive-degree Taylor term is identically zero and h=d^(-1/2) yields the supported-unit sqrt(d/n) certificate, while the isolate allowance and feasible-PC remainder remain explicit. Do not infer L=0 merely because one realized law happens to be affine while retaining honesty over the ambient positive-L class, and make no change to thm:honest-upper, thm:minimax-lower, or the main nonparametric phase diagram.
